name: 紅腹濱鷸
illustrationTaxon: Calidris canutus in breeding plumage (C. c. piersmai and C. c. rogersi are the two subspecies identified in Hong Kong, both wintering in Australasia): short-legged and slightly stockier than Great Knot, with a shorter bill that approximately equals its head length and a more greyish rump and uppertail coverts than Great Knot. In breeding plumage it has orange underparts that are richer on the male, dark grey legs, and upperparts heavily marked with black and rufous. C. c. piersmai has brick-red underparts with a reddish nape while C. c. rogersi has paler underparts often marked with black and a pale grey nape. Non-breeding birds are rather plain grey with greenish legs, and juveniles have obvious narrow dark subterminal fringes and shaft streaks with pale fringes on the wing coverts plus a buff wash to a less streaked chest. It is unobtrusive when in non-breeding plumage or in low numbers on the mudflat, and gives a short 'kyow' when foraging.

similarSpecies.distinction: 大濱鷸體型略大而更壯、嘴較厚且明顯長於頭長、腰及尾上覆羽偏白、繁殖羽只有橙褐肩羽斑而胸腹不呈磚紅色；本種嘴較短（約等於頭長）、腰偏灰、繁殖羽下身橙紅。
翻石鷸嘴短而楔形、腳橙紅、繁殖羽有黑白頭頸花紋與白色下腹；本種腳深灰綠、頭頸無黑白拼色、繁殖羽下腹橙紅。

featureNotes: 嘴長約等於頭長、基部較厚，明顯比大濱鷸的厚長嘴短（第1圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
臉頰、頸及胸為橙紅色至磚紅色，雄鳥比雌鳥更濃；後頸顏色隨亞種而異（第2圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
上背及肩羽黑、鏽紅相間並帶淡色羽緣，花紋比大濱鷸的橙褐斑塊更密更深（第3圈取自近景圖，實際可見）。
腳深灰綠色而短，站姿低矮；非繁殖羽整體轉為素灰、腳偏綠，較不起眼（第4圈取自全身圖，實際可見）。

sources.use: HKBWS substantive read: Category I, common spring passage migrant, scarce in autumn and rare in winter, with numbers in spring and autumn lower than in the 1990s; short-legged and slightly stockier than Great Knot, with a shorter bill about equal to its head length and a more greyish rump and uppertail coverts, breeding plumage with orange underparts richer on the male and dark grey legs; C. c. piersmai has brick-red underparts with a reddish nape and upperparts heavily marked black and rufous while C. c. rogersi has paler underparts often marked with black and a pale grey nape; non-breeding birds rather plain grey with greenish legs, and juveniles show obvious narrow dark subterminal fringes and shaft streaks with pale fringes on the wing coverts and a buff-washed, less streaked chest; short 'kyow' when foraging; most records from Deep Bay mudflats and adjacent Mai Po roosts, with grounded birds elsewhere only singles at Kai Tak on 29 May 1975 and 28 April 1978, a juvenile at Shuen Wan on 24 September 1994, two on a fish pond at San Tin on 20 April 2011, one at Tai Sang Wai on 19 April 2013 and two at Shui Hau, Lantau on 2 May 2020, plus up to 31 in flight over the sea in spring; primarily a spring passage migrant with lower numbers in autumn and no more than a few in winter, relatively few before the last week of March with arrivals usually obvious in early April, no counts above 20 until the final week of April this century although the 1990s had higher counts from mid-month, peak spring passage in the first half of May and most birds gone by the end of May; highest spring counts in the 1990s were 200 on 6 May 1990 and 190 on 5 May 1991 compared with peaks this century of 148 on 1 May 2020 and 123 on 4 May 2018, and systematic counts in the ten years from 1998 recorded higher peak counts than in the ten years to 2020; latest spring record five on 10 June 1989 and only three summer records; autumn passage from the last week of August with the earliest two adults on 7 August 1993, continuing to the final week of October with a small peak in the third week of September and the highest autumn count this century 14 on 20 September 2020 compared with weekly peaks of 62-93 between 30 September and 19 November 1991; apart from up to 24 in mid-November 2013 and 14 on 5 February 2010 all November to February records this century are of eight or fewer, in contrast to a peak of 80 on 9 November 1991; C. c. piersmai reported from 3 April to 4 June and C. c. rogersi from 5 April to 4 May with the former generally more numerous, juveniles in autumn from 24 August to 22 October and adults on 7 August and 7 September to 25 October; yellow northwest Australian leg-flags noted in spring and two birds ringed at Mai Po controlled at Broome; first recorded 18 May 1957; unobtrusive in non-breeding plumage or in low numbers; an Arctic breeder in north and northeast Canada, north Greenland, north central Siberia, the New Siberian Archipelago, northeast Siberia and west Alaska, wintering coastally in southern latitudes of the northern hemisphere and much of the southern hemisphere; six subspecies of which C. c. piersmai and C. c. rogersi are the most likely in Hong Kong; IUCN Near Threatened with numbers decreasing in some subpopulations including those using the East Asian-Australasian Flyway owing to habitat loss in the Yellow Sea.
HKBWS Great Knot comparison: a stockier, slightly larger bird with a thicker bill longer than the head and whitish rump, which is the key structural contrast for Red Knot.

notes: AI 生成插圖，經人眼核對短嘴約等頭長、橙紅臉頰頸胸、黑鏽相間肩羽及深灰短腳；不是照片，也不是分佈或族群證據。
兩隻比較鳥均為 AI 生成示意（大濱鷸沿用 0138 全身圖、翻石鷸沿用 0137 全身圖），非等比例；卡上不作完整鑑別檢索表。
地圖為 Natural Earth 110m 世界底圖的國家層級概述，不是精確分佈多邊形，繁殖地與越冬地不分工。
IUCN 近危 NT（黃海生境喪失令東亞—澳大拉西亞遷飛道族群下降）；香港屬 Category I，春季常見、秋季稀少、冬季罕見，春季最高 148 隻（2020-05-01），1990 年代曾達 200 隻。
